newsitem.title: USA: "Hollywood Madam" Fleiss sentenced to 37 months.
newsitem.headline: "Hollywood Madam" Fleiss sentenced to 37 months.

text.p: Reputed "Hollywood Madam" Heidi Fleiss, who ran a call-girl ring catering to the movie industry's rich and famous, was sentenced on Tuesday to 37 months in federal prison for tax evasion and money laundering.

Judge Consuelo Marshall could have sentenced her for up to nine years under federal guidelines for the eight counts on which she had been convicted. She also fined Fleiss $400 and ordered her to perform 300 hours of community service.
In a tearful appeal to the judge before sentencing, Fleiss begged for leniency, saying :"I am a different person now. I made terrible choices and mistakes."
Fleiss had been convicted in August 1995, but her sentencing was delayed after she was arrested last year for violating her bail by smoking methamphetamines.
She was recently taken into custody after completing a drug rehabilitation programme.

In addition to the federal conviction, Fleiss was also convicted in state court of pandering, but that conviction was overturned by an appelate court on the basis of jury misconduct and the judge has ordered a retrial.
